material.acceptance_criteria: One API definition (the WIT file) drives both targets: every WIT export has a wasip1 command, and a generated dispatch file is checked in CI so that adding an export without its wasip1 counterpart fails the build.
material.description: rust/crates/wasip1/src/lib.rs hand-parses text commands (tick, state, order) and rust/crates/wasip2/wit/sim-component.wit defines the component exports. No file is shared between the two targets, and no CI check ties their surfaces together, so an export added to one target drifts silently from the other.
material.resolution: wasip1 commands derive from one COMMANDS list that matches the 15 WIT exports; a CI job asserts the sets match and fails on any mismatch (printed host api ok ops=15 wasip1=15 wit=15). Protocol change: order is order <unit> <x> <y>; state is removed. Nothing else in the repo calls the old commands.
material.subject: The wasip1 guest and the wasip2 component define the host API twice
material.witness: ci-status run 38908101550 for d0d72811ae32a3288f4c5b99c91cecd2a5426e1b; host-api job 117000218777
material.witness_plan: A CI step regenerates the wasip1 dispatch from sim-component.wit and fails on any diff against the committed file, and fails when an export lacks a wasip1 command.
